qualification: Three isolated bits in CRC1/CRC2/payload of an authored32ms frame invalidate the full-frame checksum, but the native decoder ignores them and produces nonsilent PCM. The payload bit changes PCM from the clean tone, proving an actual unnoticed corruption.

The full protected frame after its syncword must have zero CRC remainder using polynomial0x8005. Failed complete frames now take the existing silence-concealment branch before frame synthesis. Partial frame and syntax concealment policy remains separate.

This is concealment acceptance: the damaged frame is intentionally silent with preserved decoded geometry/PTS, not a correct-playback acceptance for corrupted sound and not an EOF/parser refusal. CRC does not claim perfect integrity or validate every bitstream constraint.

Native actual workers verify clean sound and three silent corruptions on play/rewind/EOF seek. A combined valid-plus-bad packet preserves the good frame and conceals only the second, identical to separate source packets. Short native video control decodes.

10 AC3 decoder/6 reader units, related EOF/read-budget integrations, grouping regression, fixture reproduction and player build pass. No private inputs, encoder/network, physical DAC or measured performance claim.

A/52:2018 section7.10 leaves error response to applications and permits whole-frame CRC2 checking. The change uses the existing fvid silence policy; this is not a claim that the standard mandates rejection or silence.
compatibility: CRC-damaged AC3 frames previously decoded unchecked; they now receive existing full-frame silence concealment. Correct CRC-protected frames and public signatures remain unchanged.
counting: One missing AC3 integrity gate. CRC words, payload bit, packet grouping and playback controls add no IDs.
